title: Soft-drain optimizer and priority degradation proposal for hosted GPU pools
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a hosted API capacity exhaustion event on 2026-02-14 we observed prolonged queue buildup and bursty autoscaler activity that produced oscillatory behavior: tenants were force-drained, queues grew, and the autoscaler overcompensated which then triggered evictions and repeated cold restarts. The postmortem showed two contributing factors: (1) a hard-drain policy that dropped tenant allocations immediately during emergency shedding, and (2) autoscaler slewing thresholds tuned for throughput rather than steady-state smoothing. This ticket proposes a 'Soft-Drain Optimizer' + 'Priority Degradation' mechanism to reduce queue amplification and enable graceful capacity reductions without causing repeated cache/worker churn.
problem_statement: Hard eviction during capacity events causes cache loss and repeat requeues. Immediate drain produces cold-start latency spikes and amplifies queue length due to retries. Current autoscaler responds with aggressive scale-up followed by fast reclaim which creates oscillation and prolonged elevated latencies for many tenants.
proposal_overview: Implement a soft-drain optimizer that: (A) computes a time-windowed drain fraction per tenant (e.g., 10-60s), (B) reduces allowed concurrent slots gradually instead of immediate eviction, and (C) applies priority degradation rules that throttle lower-priority or non-latency-sensitive routes first. The optimizer will integrate with admission-control to enforce a per-tenant concurrency floor and a per-pool aggregate smoothing policy. Autoscaler will expose a slewing parameter 'scale_slew_ms' that the optimizer uses to coordinate drain windows with scaling actions.
design_details: Soft drain algorithm: when pool pressure > THRESHOLD, compute target_alloc = current_alloc * (1 - soft_drain_fraction). Apply ramp_down over ramp_window_seconds with step_size to decrement concurrent slots every step interval.

Priority degradation: Routes labelled as 'best-effort' or specific tenant tags get a degradation token bucket. When tokens exhausted, requests are delayed or routed to a lower-cost fallback model. High-priority routes are exempt unless global emergency == true.
KV cache preservation: do not evict shards with recent KV hits above a threshold; prefer shedding tenants with cold KV caches to minimize repeat token generation cost.
Autoscaler integration: expose 'planned_scale_events' to optimizer so ramp windows align with expected capacity changes, avoiding race between scale-up and immediate drain.
Observability hooks: emit events 'soft_drain_start', 'soft_drain_step', 'soft_drain_complete' with pool, tenant, and target_alloc metadata for Console dashboards and traces.
Config knobs: soft_drain_fraction (0.05-0.5), ramp_window_seconds (10-600), step_interval_seconds (1-30), priority_thresholds mapping per product tier.
Fallback: if queue length or error rate increases for protected tenants during rollout, revert to safe-mode where we pause soft-drain and rely on autoscaler for 30m.
Security considerations: no customer data is moved; privilege checks required to change per-tenant priority mappings via Console role RBAC.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces eviction-induced cache churn, lowers tail latency for high-priority tenants, smoother autoscaler behavior.
Cons: introduces additional complexity in admission control and scheduling code-paths; potential temporary throughput reduction for degraded tenants; requires thorough simulation and staged rollout.
Operational cost: small increase in control-plane metrics and observability events; modest code-surface area to maintain.
Edge cases: rapid multi-tenant surges where soft-drain cannot free capacity quickly enough — needs emergency hard-evict circuit as a last resort.
acceptance_criteria: A/ Functional: in staging chaos tests, applying a soft_drain_fraction=0.25 during a synthetic 2x throughput spike reduces average eviction rate by >= 60% compared to current hard-drain baseline.
B/ Latency: 95th percentile latency for high-priority tenants remains within 1.15x of baseline under same spike scenario.
C/ Stability: no autoscaler oscillation observed in 4/5 simulated surge scenarios when optimizer is enabled with default ramp_window_seconds=60.
D/ Observability: Console shows soft_drain events with per-tenant impact and a new chart for 'drain-induced cache misses' populated in runtime-1.22 release.
E/ Rollout: can enable via feature flag for a single pool in prod and revert safely within 15 minutes.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for ramp calculation, step scheduling, and priority token lifecycle.
2) Integration test in staging: run synthetic traffic generator (throughput and latency profiles) and compare eviction counts, queue lengths, and tail latencies vs baseline.
3) Chaos experiment: introduce node drains and GC pauses while soft-drain enabled to validate graceful behavior.
4) A/B canary: enable optimizer on a single low-risk pool for 48h, monitor key metrics and customer-error logs.
5) Performance regression bench: ensure CPU overhead on scheduler control plane < 8% for 1000 concurrent tenants.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Feature flagged dev preview: merge behind flags and land unit/integration tests. (eng-sprint 2)
Phase 1 - Staging validation: enable across 2 staging pools, run full test_plan, evaluate metrics for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 - Canary in prod: enable on a single small traffic pool for 48 hours. Escalation channel set to oncall-rl-ops.
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp: enable on remaining pools in priority order (non-enterprise -> enterprise) with 6-hour observation windows.
Phase 4 - Default on with tuned knobs; document configs in runtime-1.22 release notes and Console toggles.
Rollback: feature flag off or set soft_drain_fraction=0 instantly; safe-mode auto-triggers on p95 latency spike > 2x baseline for protected tenants.
Owner: Miguel Santos (eng), Reviewers: Priya Nair (SRE), Jordan Lee (Platform), Eva Müller (Product).
runbook_updates: Add 'soft-drain diagnostic' section describing how to read soft_drain events and how to adjust ramp_window_seconds and soft_drain_fraction in emergency.
Add step to Console incident runbook: if repeated oscillation occurs, set soft_drain_fraction=0 and raise autoscaler slew_ms to a high value while investigating.
Create checklist for pre-rollout validation and a post-rollout verification script to run after enabling the feature on a pool.
